draft.title: Language that builds rapport
card: Rapport is a feeling of connection and trust between a speaker and an audience. Speakers build it so the audience is more willing to listen and agree.
Words such as we, us and our put the speaker and audience on the same side. "We all want a safer street" treats the audience as partners, not as outsiders.
A joke about something the audience knows, or a warm, friendly tone, shows the speaker is like them. It can relax listeners and make the speaker seem likeable.
A speaker can show agreement with the audience's views, such as "You're right to be worried." This tells listeners they are understood, which can make them more open to what follows.
draft.remember: Rapport language makes the audience feel the speaker is on their side.

a.q: A principal tells students that we have all sat through a long assembly, so she will keep this one short. Which technique builds rapport here?
opts: Inclusive pronoun and a shared experience
A formal tone that keeps distance
a.why: The word we and the shared experience of long assemblies place the principal alongside the students. The formal option is wrong because it would keep a distance rather than close it.
a.clue: Look at who the speaker says is in the same situation.

b.q: Mia, a swimming coach in Geelong, begins a talk by telling her swimmers they are right that early mornings are tough, and admits she groans at her own alarm too. What effect does this most likely have on the swimmers?
opts: They feel understood, so they may listen more openly
They feel they are being told off for complaining
They feel the coach is hiding her own opinion
They feel the coach is far above them in rank
b.why: Mia agrees with the swimmers and shares a small, human admission. This shows she understands them, which can make them more open to her message. The telling-off option is wrong because she does not criticise them.
b.clue: Think about how agreement and a shared feeling make listeners feel.

a.best: Inclusive pronoun and a shared experience

b.best: They feel understood, so they may listen more openly
